This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start

- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.

- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

134	### 4.2 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` 与集成测试的 clean skip 模式
135	
136	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
137	
138	这个模块回答的问题：**集成测试怎么做到"有 GPU + 权重就真跑，没有就干净跳过"？**
139	
140	答案是一个在本 crate 23 个集成测试文件中重复出现的函数模式 `model_path_or_skip()`，配合环境变量 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH`（也是 CLAUDE.md 列出的官方测试旋钮）。它的三段式逻辑是：
141	
142	1. 环境变量设了 → 用它作为模型目录；
143	2. 没设 → 探测默认路径 `<crate>/../models/Qwen3-4B`（相对 `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`，即 crate 根的上一级 `models/` 目录）是否有 `config.json`；
144	3. 都没有 → `eprintln!` 打印一句 skip 说明，返回 `None`，测试函数直接 `return`。
145	
146	关键取舍：**skip 而不是 fail，也不是 `#[ignore]`**。skip 之后的测试会被 cargo 记为通过，但 stderr 上留下一行可检索的说明，贡献者知道这条测试存在、只是本机没权重；而 `#[ignore]` 会让测试从默认运行中彻底消失，容易被遗忘。

153	    // ……启动引擎、跑请求、断言（只有拿到 model_path 才会走到这里）

155	```

163	└─ Err 且默认路径不存在          → eprintln!("skipping qwen3 xxx: …")；None

201	### 4.3 hf_golden_gate 数值门的测试形态：绕过调度器，直接驱动 executor
202	
203	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
204	
205	这个模块回答的问题：**一个"数值正确性"集成测试长什么样，它和其他集成测试的驱动方式有何本质不同？**
206	
207	`tests/hf_golden_gate.rs` 是 Qwen3 的精度门：以 HuggingFace 为数值真值，把固定 token 序列 teacher-forcing 地回放进 pegainfer，逐位置对比 next-token logprobs。它的关键形态特征是——**完全不用 harness、不用调度器、不用 frontend**，直接拿 u1-l1 讲过的 `runtime` 再导出层：
208	
209	```rust
210	use pegainfer_qwen3::runtime::{DecodePlan, DecodeStepItem, PrefillPlan, PrefillStepItem, Qwen3Executor, RequestId};
211	```
212	
213	这印证了 u1-l1 的结论：`runtime` 再导出（[src/lib.rs:L202-L219](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L202-L219)）是本 crate 的公共执行边界——scheduler 和测试都以 plan/result 纯数据与 `Qwen3Executor` 对话。文件头部的长注释（[tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L1-L53](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L1-L53)）本身就是一份设计文档，值得整段通读。
214	
215	容差常量的深设计（为什么 mean/p99 而不是 max、margin 如何避开真平局）是 u8-l2 的主题，本讲只建立形态认知。
216	
217	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
218	
219	一次 teacher-forcing 回放（`run` 函数的 batched 分支）：
220	
221	```text
222	prefill: PrefillPlan { requests: [PrefillStepItem::new(id, prompt, …, Some(LOGPROBS))] }
223	         → execute_prefill → 每序列取 first_token_logprob，与 HF 位置 0 对比
224	循环 decode_len 次:
225	    每序列喂 golden 自己的 decode token（teacher-forcing）
226	    DecodePlan { requests: [DecodeStepItem::new(id, fed, …)] }
227	         → execute_decode → 每序列取 logprob，与 HF 位置 step+1 对比
228	收尾: 对每个 id 调 drop_request 释放 KV
229	```
230	
231	主测试函数把多个"pass"塞进**一个** `#[test]` 里顺序执行：bs=1 顺序回放（+ 重复一次做逐位确定性断言）、batched eager（跨请求隔离检查）、prefix-cache 冷/热回放、CUDA-graph 桶跨越批（batch 9→桶 16、5→桶 8，最大化 padding 槽位）、以及 ≥2 GPU 时的 TP=2 全套重放。
232	
233	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
234	
235	**构造 plan item 的两个小工厂。** [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L374-L387](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L374-L387)：`prefill_item` / `decode_item` 把 prompt（或被喂入的 token）包成 `PrefillStepItem` / `DecodeStepItem`，都请求 `Some(LOGPROBS)`（64 个 top logprob，让 pegainfer 的 top-K 与 HF 夹具的 top-K 有交集）。
236	
237	**回放主循环。** [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L396-L486](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L396-L486) 的 `run` 是核心：`batched = false` 逐序列单独跑（bs=1，最紧对比），`batched = true` 时先给所有序列发 prefill（L413-L418 直接调 `ex.execute_prefill(PrefillPlan { sample_seed: 0, requests: &items })`），然后每步给所有序列发 decode（L434-L439），teacher-forcing 体现在 L432——喂的是 `g.decode(s, step)`，即 golden 夹具自己的第 `step` 个"标准答案" token，不是 pegainfer 采样的结果。函数还顺手返回一个 fingerprint（pegainfer 每个位置自己的 top-1 logprob），供外部断言两次同输入运行**逐位相同**（[L564-L570](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L564-L570)）。
238	
239	**为什么只有一个 `#[test]`。** [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L606-L634](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L606-L634)：注释写明"每个 executor 独占 GPU 显存；用作用域保证同时只有一个模型驻留……所有内容放在一个 `#[test]` 里也是同一原因：两个并行测试会各自为 KV 预算 85% 的空闲显存"。cargo 默认并行跑测试线程，对会瓜分显存的 GPU 测试来说并行=自杀，所以整个门是一根顺序执行的长链。
240	
241	**图 pass 的资格门。** [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L639-L663](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L639-L663)：CUDA-graph 回放只在"该模型的 GQA group 有编译好的解码核"时执行（判定函数在 [L168-L185](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L168-L185)，查 `pegainfer_core::ops::SUPPORTED_GQA_GROUP_SIZES`）；否则打印说明、跳过图 pass（例：Qwen3-14B 的 group 5 未编译）。

258	
259	**练习 1**：teacher-forcing 与自由贪心对比，各自适合验证什么？
260	**答案**：自由贪心一旦某步 argmax 翻转，两条序列从此分岔，只能比最终文本，定位不了出错位置；teacher-forcing 每步喂同一固定 token，两个引擎在每个位置输入完全相同，可以逐位置断言分布（margin/mean/p99）。它牺牲了"端到端生成质量"的覆盖，换取可归因的数值定位。

268	### 4.4 `tests/common/harness.rs`：把 step 批量协议还原成每请求阻塞流
269	
270	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
271	
272	这个模块回答的问题：**集成测试怎么方便地"提交一个请求、阻塞等它生成完"？**
273	
274	引擎契约（pegainfer-frontend 的 `Engine`）对外吐的是**按 step 批量**的更新流：每个 step 一批 `RequestUpdate`，不同请求的更新混在同一批里。而集成测试的人体工程学是老的"每请求一条流"——`submit` 之后逐条 `recv`，直到 `Finished`。[tests/common/harness.rs:L1-L7](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L1-L7) 的文件头注释说得直白：集成测试早于 step 批量协议存在，这个泵用**生产桥同款方式**（一个线程把 `StepOutputs` 解复用进每请求队列）恢复了旧人体工程学，且全程同步——GPU 测试就在普通测试线程上驱动请求。
275	
276	为什么这个文件放在 `tests/common/` 且每个测试文件都要 `mod common;`？因为 cargo 的集成测试每个文件是独立 crate，公共代码只能以模块源码的形式被各自编译一次（[tests/common/mod.rs:L1](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/mod.rs#L1) 的 `pub(crate) mod harness;`）。[tests/common/harness.rs:L9-L11](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L9-L11) 因此标了 `#![allow(dead_code)]`——每个测试 crate 只用这个模块的一部分，未用的部分不该报警。
277	
278	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
279	
280	夹具的生命周期：
281	
282	```text
283	EngineHarness::new(engine)
284	    ├─ 断言 engine.schedulers.len() == 1（测试只驱动单调度器引擎）
285	    ├─ scheduler.handle.take_steps()   ← 每个 scheduler 的 step 流只能被取走一次
286	    ├─ 建立 Inbox { updates: HashMap<RequestId, VecDeque<RequestUpdate>>, closed } + Condvar
287	    └─ spawn 泵线程:
288	         while let Some(step) = steps.blocking_recv():
289	             把 step.updates 按 update.id 分发进各自队列 → notify_all
290	         流关闭后: closed = true → notify_all
291	
292	submit(request) → RequestStream { id, control, inbox }
293	RequestStream::recv()  → 锁 Inbox；自己队列有则弹出，否则在 Condvar 上等待
294	RequestStream::outcome() → 反复 recv，折叠 tokens/logprobs，直到 terminal
295	RequestStream::expect_finished() → outcome + 要求 Terminal::Finished，否则 panic
296	
297	Drop（夹具销毁）
298	    ├─ drop(handle)  → 关闭提交通道，scheduler 排干并退出
299	    ├─ join(scheduler线程) → step 流随之关闭
300	    └─ join(泵线程)        → 泵检测 closed，退出
301	```
302	
303	#### 4.4.3 源码精读
304	
305	**默认请求工厂。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L37-L65](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L37-L65)：`request(prompt_tokens, params, max_tokens)` 填一份"测试默认"的 `Request`——无 LoRA、无 logprobs、无历史、EOS 策略随采样参数。注释点明用法：要测 prompt-logprob / LoRA 变体，就在返回值上改字段。
306	
307	**夹具结构。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L67-L74](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L67-L74)：`EngineHarness` 持有 scheduler 句柄、LoRA 客户端、scheduler 与泵两个线程的 JoinHandle、共享 Inbox，以及引擎的 `EngineInfo`。
308	
309	**构造与泵线程。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L87-L130](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L87-L130)：`new` 先断言单调度器（L88-L92），`take_steps()` 拿走 step 流（L94-L97，"新鲜的 scheduler 只让出一次"），然后 spawn 泵线程（L106-L121）——`blocking_recv` 收一个 step，把其中每条 update 按其 `id` 塞进 `HashMap` 里对应的 `VecDeque`，解锁后 `notify_all`；流结束时置 `closed = true` 再 `notify_all`。
310	
311	**提交与便捷方法。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L132-L143](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L132-L143)：`submit` 经 scheduler 句柄提交请求，返回绑定了请求 id 与 Inbox 的 `RequestStream`。[tests/common/harness.rs:L160-L169](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L160-L169) 的 `generate` 是"大多数 GPU 测试要的形状"：提交、折叠到 Finished、直接返回 token 序列。
312	
313	**每请求视图。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L200-L215](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L200-L215)：`recv` 是教科书式的 Condvar 循环——锁内先试弹出自己的队列，弹到就返回；`closed` 就返回 `None`；否则 `wait` 让出锁等待泵的 `notify_all`。`RequestStream` 是 `Send` 的（L186-L187 注释），所以并发请求可以从不同测试线程各自驱动。
314	
315	**折叠与终止。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L219-L262](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L219-L262)：`outcome` 循环 recv，把 tokens / logprobs 累积进 `Outcome`（结构见 [L267-L273](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L267-L273)），并断言 `cached_tokens` 至多上报一次（L237-L243——这本身就是在钉一条引擎契约，u5-l1 的 cached_tokens_usage 测试依赖它）；拿到 `terminal` 即返回。`expect_finished` 在 L255-L262：`Rejected`/`Failed` 一律 panic——对测试而言"引擎拒绝"不是一种可接受的结果，而是一次失败。
316	
317	**有序关闭。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L172-L184](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L172-L184)：`Drop` 的注释把因果链写全了——关提交通道 → scheduler 排干退出 → step 流关闭 → 泵收尾。顺序 join 两个线程，保证测试进程不会留下悬挂线程。
318	
319	**日志开关。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L279-L302](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L279-L302)：cargo 的测试二进制默认不装 logger；`init_capture_logging` 在 `PEGAINFER_TEST_LOG=1` 时装一个只转发 `pegainfer_qwen3` 目标的最小 stderr logger——投机解码的负载门测试（`tests/dflash_speculative_gate.rs`，u6-l7）靠数子进程 stderr 上的 hedge trace 行来断言，多余的日志会污染解析。

321	**一个完整的调用方样例。** [tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs:L55-L104](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs#L55-L104) 展示了夹具的完整用法链：`model_path_or_skip()` → `pegainfer_qwen3::start_engine(Path::new(&model_path), EngineLoadOptions { enable_cuda_graph: true, device_ordinals: vec![0], seed: 42, .. })`（`start_engine` 定义在 [src/lib.rs:L354-L366](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L354-L366)，它只是带默认参数转发到 `start_engine_with_offload`）→ `EngineHarness::new(engine)` → `common::load_tokenizer(&model_path)` 编码 prompt → `engine.submit(request(...)).expect_finished()` 折叠结果并断言 `cached_tokens`。tokenizer 装载在 [tests/common/mod.rs:L14-L40](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/mod.rs#L14-L40)，按模型目录自动挑 HF / Tiktoken / Tekken 三种后端。

323	#### 4.4.4 代码实践
324	
325	**实践目标**：在纸面上跟踪一次 `generate` 调用的完整数据流，确认你理解泵的存在意义。
326	
327	**操作步骤**：
328	
329	1. 从 [tests/common/harness.rs:L160-L169](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L160-L169) 的 `generate` 出发，依次列出涉及的结构：`request()` → `submit()` → `RequestStream` → `recv()`/`outcome()` → `Outcome.tokens`。
330	2. 画一张时序图，三条竖线：测试线程、泵线程、scheduler。标出 `submit`、每个 step 的 `blocking_recv` → 队列分发 → `notify_all` → 测试线程 `wait` 醒来取数据、以及 `Terminal` 到达和夹具 `Drop` 时的关闭顺序。
331	3. 思考并回答：如果没有泵线程、测试线程直接 `blocking_recv` step 流，会发生什么？
332	
333	**需要观察的现象 / 预期结果**：第 3 步的答案——测试线程会拿到**所有请求混在一起**的批量更新，得自己按 id 过滤；请求一多，"等某个特定请求的下一条"没有阻塞原语可用。泵把"按 id 分发 + 等待"封装进 `Inbox`+`Condvar`，测试侧就回到每请求一条流的直觉。
334	
335	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
336	
337	**练习 1**：`EngineHarness::new` 为什么断言 `engine.schedulers.len() == 1`？
338	**答案**：夹具只从一个 scheduler 取 step 流、Inbox 也只解复用这一条流；多调度器（多模型线/多设备拓扑）的引擎不适用这个简化夹具（[tests/common/harness.rs:L88-L92](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L88-L92)）。
339	
340	**练习 2**：`recv` 在什么情况下返回 `None`？`outcome` 为什么把它当作 panic 而不是正常结束？
341	**答案**：`None` 只在 `closed == true`（引擎侧流已关闭）时出现（[L210-L212](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L210-L212)）。正常路径下每个请求必以一个 `terminal` 更新收尾；流先于 terminal 关闭意味着引擎死掉，对测试是失败而非结果（`outcome` 里的 `expect`，[L232-L234](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L232-L234)）。
342	
343	**练习 3**：`Drop` 里如果先 join 泵线程、后 drop handle，会发生什么？
344	**答案**：泵线程在 `blocking_recv` 上等下一个 step，而 scheduler 要等提交通道关闭才会排干退出——通道由 `handle` 持有，不先 drop 它泵永远收不到流关闭，join 死锁。所以顺序必须是 drop handle → join scheduler → join 泵（[L172-L184](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L172-L184) 注释原文即此因果链）。

346	## 5. 综合实践：写一个最小集成测试骨架

348	**任务**：通读 `tests/common/harness.rs` 与任一集成测试的 skip 分支后，亲手写一个最小集成测试骨架——复用 harness 的 submit/pump 语义，无 GPU 时 clean skip——并验证它编译通过、且不破坏 crate 的 lib 目标。

388	    };

# 运行与测试地图：单测、GPU 集成测试与测试夹具

> 本讲属于单元 u1「起步：认识 pegainfer-qwen3」，承接 u1-l1 建立的模块地图与 plan/result 相位边界概念。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 分清 pegainfer-qwen3 的两类测试——`--lib` 单元测试（不需要 GPU）与 `tests/` 下的集成测试（需要 CUDA GPU + 模型权重）——并知道如何分别运行它们。
2. 理解 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` 环境变量与"clean skip"模式：为什么缺权重时测试是跳过而不是失败。
3. 读懂 `tests/common/harness.rs`：它如何用一个泵线程把引擎的 step 批量输出协议还原成"每个请求一条阻塞流"的旧式测试人体工程学，并能照它的样子写出一个最小集成测试骨架。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 cargo 的两类测试目标

Rust/cargo 把测试分成两类编译目标（target）：

- **单元测试**：写在 `src/` 源码内部、标了 `#[cfg(test)]` 的模块里。它们和库本体一起编译，只在 `cargo test` 时启用，平时不占产物体积。`cargo test --lib` 只编译并运行这一类。
- **集成测试**：`tests/` 目录下每个 `*.rs` 文件都是一个**独立的 crate**，只能通过库的公共 API（`pub` 项）访问被测代码。`cargo test --test <文件名>` 只运行其中一个。

这个区分对本 crate 尤其重要：单元测试测的是纯函数（配置解析、调度装箱、旋钮解析……），**不需要 GPU**；集成测试要真正建起一个 `Qwen3Executor`、装载权重、跑前向，**必须有 CUDA GPU 和模型权重**。

### 2.2 `cfg(test)` 与 feature 的关系

`#[cfg(test)]` 只在编译**库自身测试目标**时为真。集成测试是另一个 crate，它 `use pegainfer_qwen3::...` 时库是以"普通被依赖方"身份编译的，`cfg(test)` 为假。所以"想给集成测试暴露的测试辅助代码"必须走别的门——本 crate 用了一个空 feature `test-fixtures` 来当这扇门，见 4.1.3。

### 2.3 为什么推理引擎的测试要"分层"

模型 crate 的代码里，很大一部分逻辑（配置校验、队列装箱、纯决策级联）是纯 CPU 数据变换，可以在任何机器上快速验证；而数值正确性（logits 是否和 HuggingFace 对得上）和行为契约（取消、前缀缓存命中上报）必须真的在 GPU 上跑。把它们分开意味着：**没有 GPU 的贡献者也能跑通绝大多数回归**，GPU 测试则留给 CI 或本地显卡机器。

### 2.4 你需要的几个背景术语

- **prefill / decode**：u1-l1 已建立的两阶段概念——先整段吃进 prompt（prefill），再逐 token 生成（decode）。
- **teacher-forcing（教师强制）**：解码时不采信模型自己生成的下一个 token，而是喂入预先固定好的"标准答案" token，让每一步的输入完全确定，从而两个引擎（HF 与 pegainfer）在每个位置上看到完全相同的输入，可以逐位置对比分布。
- **bf16 与 ULP**：bfloat16 是截短尾数的浮点格式，一次 GEMM 的求和顺序不同就会让最低几位（Unit in the Last Place，ULP）漂移。这是本讲 4.3 中"为什么不用逐位快照对比"的根源，深度设计留给 u8-l2。
- **生产者-消费者与 Condvar**：一个线程往队列里放数据并 `notify_all`，另一个线程锁住、检查队列、为空则 `wait` 挂起——`harness.rs` 的核心就是这样一个解复用器。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲按四个最小模块展开：**(1) `--lib` 单测入口与 Cargo 测试目标体系**、**(2) `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` 与 clean skip 模式**、**(3) hf_golden_gate 数值门的测试形态**、**(4) `tests/common/harness.rs` 阻塞式引擎泵**。

### 4.1 `--lib` 单测入口与 Cargo 测试目标体系

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

这个模块回答的问题：**没有 GPU 的机器上，这个 crate 能测什么、怎么测？**

pegainfer-qwen3 的 28 处 `#[cfg(test)]` 模块遍布 `src/`——config（配置校验）、scheduler 与 scheduler/plan（队列装箱、执行计划）、spec_env（环境旋钮解析）、executor/spec（投机解码纯逻辑）、lora（适配器解析）等。它们测的都是**纯数据变换**：输入一个结构体或一段文本，断言输出，完全不碰 CUDA。运行入口就是：

```bash
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib
```

注意 `--release`：CLAUDE.md 明确要求所有构建都用 release（debug 下 GPU/CUDA 相关代码极慢，虽然 `--lib` 单测不跑 GPU，但编译整个依赖树时 debug 也慢得多）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib` 的执行流程：

1. cargo 以 `cfg(test)` 编译 `pegainfer-qwen3` 库目标本身（连带 dev-dependencies，且 dev-dependency 里声明的 feature 一并启用，见下）。
2. 收集所有 `#[test]` 函数，生成测试执行器。
3. 顺序/并行运行，全部不触碰 GPU。

与集成测试的关系：

```text
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3            # lib 单测 + 所有 tests/*.rs 集成测试
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib      # 仅 lib 单测（无 GPU 可跑）
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate   # 仅一个集成测试 crate
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**features 与自引用 dev-dependency。** [Cargo.toml:L34-L45](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/Cargo.toml#L34-L45) 声明了三个 feature：`kernel-call-trace`、`kernel-report`（诊断工具链，拉起一组可选依赖）和 `test-fixtures = []`——一个**空 feature**，唯一作用是当一个编译期开关。[Cargo.toml:L47-L51](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/Cargo.toml#L47-L51) 是关键一招：dev-dependencies 里把**自己**列了进来，并启用 `test-fixtures`：

```toml
[dev-dependencies]
pegainfer-qwen3 = { workspace = true, features = ["test-fixtures"] }
```

这利用了 cargo 的 feature 合并规则：集成测试 crate（`tests/*.rs`）通过这条 dev-dependency 依赖库时，库会带着 `test-fixtures` 编译。库这边对应的门在 [src/lib.rs:L14-L15](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L14-L15)：

```rust
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-fixtures"))]
pub use lora::fixtures as lora_fixtures;
```

这行代码的意思：编译库自身测试（`test` cfg 为真）**或** `test-fixtures` feature 打开时，把 LoRA 测试夹具（伪造的适配器权重等）导出为公共 API。于是：单元测试天然可见，集成测试通过 dev-dependency 的 feature 也可见，而普通用户的构建里它根本不存在。

**内联单测样例。** [src/spec_env.rs:L53-L65](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/spec_env.rs#L53-L65) 是最小形态——文件底部一个 `mod tests`，断言"空串/空白/`0` 都解析为 off，非法值报错时要带上变量名"。这是本 crate 单测的平均样子：短、快、无 GPU。

**独立文件的单测组织。** 测试多起来时，本 crate 的惯例是把测试挪到同名文件。[src/scheduler.rs:L578-L581](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler.rs#L578-L581) 声明了两个只在测试期编译的子模块——`test_support`（测试要用的辅助构造器）和 `tests`（测试本体，位于 `src/scheduler/tests.rs`）。后续 u4 系列讲义会大量阅读这两个文件。

**feature 门控的二进制。** [Cargo.toml:L53-L61](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/Cargo.toml#L53-L61) 声明了 `qwen3_kernel_report` / `qwen3_model_report` 两个诊断二进制，`required-features = ["kernel-report"]` 表示不带 `--features kernel-report` 时它们不会被构建（u8-l3 专门讲）。另外 [Cargo.toml:L2](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/Cargo.toml#L2) 的 `autobenches = false` 关闭了 bench 目标的自动发现，bench 走 `pegainfer-bench` 那条线。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：在没有 GPU 的机器上确认 lib 单测可运行、并看清单测都藏在哪些模块里。

**操作步骤**：

1. 在仓库根目录运行 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib`。
2. 再运行 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib -- --list`，把列出的测试按文件名前缀归组。
3. 对照本节列出的 `#[cfg(test)]` 位置（可用 `grep -n "cfg(test)" -r src/` 复核）。

**需要观察的现象**：`--list` 输出里的测试全部来自 `src/` 下的模块（config、scheduler、spec_env、lora……），没有任何一条需要装载权重；测试运行总时长很短（工作区文档对整套 `--workspace --lib` 的标注约 9 秒）。

**预期结果**：全部通过。**待本地验证**（本讲义写作环境未执行 cargo）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `test-fixtures` 必须是 feature，而不能直接 `#[cfg(test)]`？
**答案**：`cfg(test)` 只在编译库自身的测试目标时为真；`tests/` 下的集成测试是独立 crate，它看到的库是普通依赖，`cfg(test)` 为假。空 feature + dev-dependency 自引用（[Cargo.toml:L48](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/Cargo.toml#L48)）让集成测试编译时该门为真，而用户构建不受影响。

**练习 2**：`cargo test -p pegainfer-qwen3`（不带 `--lib`）和 `--lib` 的区别是什么？
**答案**：前者还会编译并运行 `tests/` 下全部 24 个集成测试文件；这些测试大多需要 GPU + 权重，缺权重时它们会走 skip 分支（见 4.2）而非失败，但编译整个测试集仍比 `--lib` 慢。

**练习 3**：`src/scheduler.rs` 里 `test_support` 与 `tests` 两个子模块为什么不直接内联在 `scheduler.rs` 里？
**答案**：把测试与测试辅助拆到 `src/scheduler/tests.rs` / `test_support.rs` 独立文件，避免主源码文件被几百行测试代码撑爆；`#[cfg(test)]` 保证它们不进入正式产物。这是大模块（如 scheduler、weights）的通用惯例。

### 4.2 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` 与集成测试的 clean skip 模式

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

这个模块回答的问题：**集成测试怎么做到"有 GPU + 权重就真跑，没有就干净跳过"？**

答案是一个在本 crate 23 个集成测试文件中重复出现的函数模式 `model_path_or_skip()`，配合环境变量 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH`（也是 CLAUDE.md 列出的官方测试旋钮）。它的三段式逻辑是：

1. 环境变量设了 → 用它作为模型目录；
2. 没设 → 探测默认路径 `<crate>/../models/Qwen3-4B`（相对 `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`，即 crate 根的上一级 `models/` 目录）是否有 `config.json`；
3. 都没有 → `eprintln!` 打印一句 skip 说明，返回 `None`，测试函数直接 `return`。

关键取舍：**skip 而不是 fail，也不是 `#[ignore]`**。skip 之后的测试会被 cargo 记为通过，但 stderr 上留下一行可检索的说明，贡献者知道这条测试存在、只是本机没权重；而 `#[ignore]` 会让测试从默认运行中彻底消失，容易被遗忘。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
#[test] fn xxx() {
    let Some(model_path) = model_path_or_skip() else { return; };   // ← 每个 GPU 测试的第一行
    // ……启动引擎、跑请求、断言（只有拿到 model_path 才会走到这里）
}
```

`model_path_or_skip()` 内部：

```text
读取 PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH
├─ Ok(path)                     → Some(path)
├─ Err 且 <manifest>/../models/Qwen3-4B/config.json 存在 → Some(默认路径)
└─ Err 且默认路径不存在          → eprintln!("skipping qwen3 xxx: …")；None
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**标准实现。** [tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs:L24-L37](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs#L24-L37) 是这个模式的最干净样例：`match std::env::var(...)` 的三臂分别对应上面流程图的三个分支。默认路径常量在 [tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs:L21](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs#L21)，用 `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../models/Qwen3-4B")` 在编译期拼出绝对路径——不依赖当前工作目录，测试从任何目录启动都有效。调用侧在 [tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs:L57-L59](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs#L57-L59)：`let Some(model_path) = model_path_or_skip() else { return; }`——let-else 一行完成"跳过即返回"。

**同一函数在 hf_golden_gate 里的版本。** [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L116-L129](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L116-L129) 与上一段逐字同构，只是 skip 文案换成该测试自己的名字。

**skip 的第二层：golden 夹具缺失。** hf_golden_gate 还需要第二份输入——HF 参考分布夹具。夹具按模型尺寸命名，[tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L138-L159](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L138-L159) 用 `(hidden_size, num_hidden_layers)` 几何查尺寸表（如 `(2560, 36)` → `"4b"`）；[tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L291-L321](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L291-L321) 在几何查不到、或该尺寸的 `test_data/qwen3-{size}-hf-golden.safetensors` 不存在且不在已提交清单里时，同样打印说明并返回 `None`（若设了 `PEGAINFER_QWEN3_HF_GOLDEN` 环境变量则强制从该路径读，查不到几何直接 assert 失败——显式指定却对不上，是配置错误而非缺资源）。

**skip 的第三层：GPU 数量。** [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L668-L673](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L668-L673) 在可见 CUDA 设备少于 2 个时跳过 TP=2 对照组（设备数探测在 [tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L543-L545](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L543-L545)，驱动都查不到时按 0 处理）。

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：亲眼确认"无权重时集成测试 skip 而不 fail"。

**操作步骤**：

1. 确认没有设置 `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH`，且 `<仓库>/models/Qwen3-4B/config.json` 不存在。
2. 运行 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test cached_tokens_usage -- --nocapture`。
3. 把某个含 `config.json` 的目录指给环境变量，重跑同一条命令。

**需要观察的现象**：第 2 步 stderr 打印 `skipping qwen3 cached_tokens_usage: ... set PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH to run it`，测试结果为 ok（函数提前返回）；第 3 步则会真正尝试装载（随后可能因目录里没有完整权重而失败——这是预期行为，说明它已越过 skip 分支）。

**预期结果**：skip 分支零失败。**待本地验证**。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么默认模型路径用 `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` 拼接，而不是相对路径 `"../models/Qwen3-4B"`？
**答案**：集成测试二进制的运行时工作目录不一定是 crate 根（cargo 以 crate 根为 cwd 运行测试，但 `--target-dir`、外部调用等情况下不保证）；`env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` 在编译期固化为绝对路径，与运行目录无关（见 [tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs:L21](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/cached_tokens_usage.rs#L21)）。

**练习 2**：`model_path_or_skip` 探测的是 `config.json` 存在性而不是 `*.safetensors`，会不会出现"探测通过但后面装载失败"？
**答案**：会。`config.json` 是"这里像一份模型"的最低门槛（hf_golden_gate 还用它读几何，见 L138 起），完整权重缺失会在引擎启动阶段以错误暴露。skip 只负责"明显没模型"这一层，目录残缺属于应该报错的场景。

**练习 3**：为什么不把这些测试标 `#[ignore]`，要用运行时 skip？
**答案**：`#[ignore]` 的测试默认根本不运行，久了没人记得开；运行时 skip 让测试始终出现在结果里，且 stderr 说明"怎样才能跑起来"，对新贡献者是一份活文档。

### 4.3 hf_golden_gate 数值门的测试形态：绕过调度器，直接驱动 executor

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

这个模块回答的问题：**一个"数值正确性"集成测试长什么样，它和其他集成测试的驱动方式有何本质不同？**

`tests/hf_golden_gate.rs` 是 Qwen3 的精度门：以 HuggingFace 为数值真值，把固定 token 序列 teacher-forcing 地回放进 pegainfer，逐位置对比 next-token logprobs。它的关键形态特征是——**完全不用 harness、不用调度器、不用 frontend**，直接拿 u1-l1 讲过的 `runtime` 再导出层：

```rust
use pegainfer_qwen3::runtime::{DecodePlan, DecodeStepItem, PrefillPlan, PrefillStepItem, Qwen3Executor, RequestId};
```

这印证了 u1-l1 的结论：`runtime` 再导出（[src/lib.rs:L202-L219](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L202-L219)）是本 crate 的公共执行边界——scheduler 和测试都以 plan/result 纯数据与 `Qwen3Executor` 对话。文件头部的长注释（[tests/hf_golden_gate.rs:L1-L53](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/hf_golden_gate.rs#L1-L53)）本身就是一份设计文档，值得整段通读。

容差常量的深设计（为什么 mean/p99 而不是 max、margin 如何避开真平局）是 u8-l2 的主题，本讲只建立形态认知。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

一次 teacher-forcing 回放（`run` 函数的 batched 分支）：

```text
prefill: PrefillPlan { requests: [PrefillStepItem::new(id, prompt, …, Some(LOGPROBS))] }
         → execute_prefill → 每序列取 first_token_logprob，与 HF 位置 0 对比
循环 decode_len 次:
    每序列喂 golden 自己的 decode token（teacher-forcing）
    DecodePlan { requests: [DecodeStepItem::new(id, fed, …)] }
         → execute_decode → 每序列取 logprob，与 HF 位置 step+1 对比
收尾: 对每个 id 调 drop_request 释放 KV
```

主测试函数把多个"pass"塞进**一个** `#[test]` 里顺序执行：bs=1 顺序回放（+ 重复一次做逐位确定性断言）、batched eager（跨请求隔离检查）、prefix-cache 冷/热回放、CUDA-graph 桶跨越批（batch 9→桶 16、5→桶 8，最大化 padding 槽位）、以及 ≥2 GPU 时的 TP=2 全套重放。

**练习 1**：teacher-forcing 与自由贪心对比，各自适合验证什么？

### 4.4 `tests/common/harness.rs`：把 step 批量协议还原成每请求阻塞流

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

这个模块回答的问题：**集成测试怎么方便地"提交一个请求、阻塞等它生成完"？**

引擎契约（pegainfer-frontend 的 `Engine`）对外吐的是**按 step 批量**的更新流：每个 step 一批 `RequestUpdate`，不同请求的更新混在同一批里。而集成测试的人体工程学是老的"每请求一条流"——`submit` 之后逐条 `recv`，直到 `Finished`。[tests/common/harness.rs:L1-L7](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L1-L7) 的文件头注释说得直白：集成测试早于 step 批量协议存在，这个泵用**生产桥同款方式**（一个线程把 `StepOutputs` 解复用进每请求队列）恢复了旧人体工程学，且全程同步——GPU 测试就在普通测试线程上驱动请求。

为什么这个文件放在 `tests/common/` 且每个测试文件都要 `mod common;`？因为 cargo 的集成测试每个文件是独立 crate，公共代码只能以模块源码的形式被各自编译一次（[tests/common/mod.rs:L1](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/mod.rs#L1) 的 `pub(crate) mod harness;`）。[tests/common/harness.rs:L9-L11](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L9-L11) 因此标了 `#![allow(dead_code)]`——每个测试 crate 只用这个模块的一部分，未用的部分不该报警。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

夹具的生命周期：

```text
EngineHarness::new(engine)
    ├─ 断言 engine.schedulers.len() == 1（测试只驱动单调度器引擎）
    ├─ scheduler.handle.take_steps()   ← 每个 scheduler 的 step 流只能被取走一次
    ├─ 建立 Inbox { updates: HashMap<RequestId, VecDeque<RequestUpdate>>, closed } + Condvar
    └─ spawn 泵线程:
         while let Some(step) = steps.blocking_recv():
             把 step.updates 按 update.id 分发进各自队列 → notify_all
         流关闭后: closed = true → notify_all

submit(request) → RequestStream { id, control, inbox }
RequestStream::recv()  → 锁 Inbox；自己队列有则弹出，否则在 Condvar 上等待
RequestStream::outcome() → 反复 recv，折叠 tokens/logprobs，直到 terminal
RequestStream::expect_finished() → outcome + 要求 Terminal::Finished，否则 panic

Drop（夹具销毁）
    ├─ drop(handle)  → 关闭提交通道，scheduler 排干并退出
    ├─ join(scheduler线程) → step 流随之关闭
    └─ join(泵线程)        → 泵检测 closed，退出
```

#### 4.4.3 源码精读

**默认请求工厂。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L37-L65](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L37-L65)：`request(prompt_tokens, params, max_tokens)` 填一份"测试默认"的 `Request`——无 LoRA、无 logprobs、无历史、EOS 策略随采样参数。注释点明用法：要测 prompt-logprob / LoRA 变体，就在返回值上改字段。

**夹具结构。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L67-L74](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L67-L74)：`EngineHarness` 持有 scheduler 句柄、LoRA 客户端、scheduler 与泵两个线程的 JoinHandle、共享 Inbox，以及引擎的 `EngineInfo`。

**构造与泵线程。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L87-L130](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L87-L130)：`new` 先断言单调度器（L88-L92），`take_steps()` 拿走 step 流（L94-L97，"新鲜的 scheduler 只让出一次"），然后 spawn 泵线程（L106-L121）——`blocking_recv` 收一个 step，把其中每条 update 按其 `id` 塞进 `HashMap` 里对应的 `VecDeque`，解锁后 `notify_all`；流结束时置 `closed = true` 再 `notify_all`。

**每请求视图。** [tests/common/harness.rs:L200-L215](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/785d04871df37ddfb3e1b1432ce544b94505a801/pegainfer-qwen3/tests/common/harness.rs#L200-L215)：`recv` 是教科书式的 Condvar 循环——锁内先试弹出自己的队列，弹到就返回；`closed` 就返回 `None`；否则 `wait` 让出锁等待泵的 `notify_all`。`RequestStream` 是 `Send` 的（L186-L187 注释），所以并发请求可以从不同测试线程各自驱动。

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
